name: sol_ec_5
description: Arbitrary/untrusted external call target not restricted to a whitelist
question: The source file in `source` defines a function that performs a low-level external call, delegatecall, or invokes an arbitrary target/contract address supplied via user or caller-controlled input, without validating that address against a whitelist, allowlist, or hardcoded set of trusted addresses, allowing an attacker to redirect the call to a malicious contract and steal funds or hijack execution; this excludes calls to addresses that are fixed constants, immutable values set only by a trusted admin at deployment, or already validated against an on-chain allowlist/registry before the call.
criteria: A bridge/facet function takes a 'callTo' or 'target' parameter from calldata and executes call(target, data) without checking target against any allowlist
A swap/router function accepts an arbitrary 'dex' or 'pool' address argument and forwards call{value: amount}(dex, data) without verifying dex is a trusted registered exchange
A function reads a destination or relayer address from user input and issues a delegatecall to it without comparing it to a stored list of approved addresses
A cross-chain messaging function forwards execution to an address parameter supplied in the payload without hardcoding or checking it against a trusted gateway/adapter address
